Extraction: A Joint Study of the Challenges, Opportunities, and Roadmap of MLOps and AIOps: A Systematic Survey
Josu Diaz-de-Arcaya; Ana I. Torre-Bastida; Gorka Zárate; Raúl Miñón; Aitor Almeida
2023; ACM Computing Surveys (ACM Comput. Surv.), Vol. 56, No. 4, Article 84, October 2023; DOI 10.1145/3625289

Operationalizing data science/AI projects in production is far harder than pure software engineering, and organizations struggle to convert data-science insights into business value; the young MLOps and AIOps paradigms lack a joint, systematic understanding of their open issues, opportunities, frameworks, and application fields, which hinders wider adoption in industry and academia (Sec. 1, pp. 2-3; Sec. 1.2, pp. 3-4)

No system or agent is proposed; this is a survey that jointly maps MLOps and AIOps around five research questions (challenges, MLOps trends, AIOps trends, frameworks/architectures, application fields) and proposes a comparison framework (Table 1) where AIOps aims to "reduce human intervention" and build "self-learning and self-healing applications" for IT (Sec. 1.1, Table 1, p. 3; Table 2, p. 4); it surveys AIOps roles in anomaly detection, root cause analysis via logs, proactive incident triage/remediation, KPI degradation inference, and resource management (Sec. 4.3.1, p. 15; Sec. 4.4.1, p. 17; Sec. 4.5, pp. 19-20). No agentic AI, multi-agent, or LLM-copilot architecture is used; LLMs appear only as an emerging concern/opportunity (Sec. 4.1.4, p. 12; Sec. 4.2.2, p. 14)

Systematic Literature Review following Kitchenham-style guidelines [65] and PRISMA reporting; automated retrieval via a custom Scopus API client (code on GitHub); 600 search strings from topic/action/dimension term combinations plus a dedicated AIOps query; window 2018-2023; 44,903 records identified, 23,508 passed to screening, 21,940 excluded by title and 1,111 by abstract, 452 full papers downloaded, 93 studies included; quality appraisal with 7 weighted metrics scoring 0-10 (Sec. 2, pp. 4-6; Sec. 3.1, pp. 7-8, Fig. 3, Table 5; Table 4, p. 7)

Not specified — no MTTD/MTTR/alert-fatigue numbers are reported. Qualitative only: AIOps thrives in proactive and reactive failure management ("prevention, prediction, detection, root cause analysis, remediation") (Sec. 4.5.1, p. 19); AIOps in ITSM shows "potential for predicting and resolving IT incidents in the shortest time" [1] (Sec. 4.5.2, p. 20); log analysis supports incident remediation [76, 86] and data-driven proactive incident triage [76] (Sec. 4.5.2, p. 20; Sec. 4.4.1, p. 17)

Field: General Impact on Agentic AI / Multi-Agent Systems
Extraction: Not applicable — no agentic or multi-agent systems are evaluated. Related findings: prior work observes that in AIOps "many of the solutions focus on detection and root cause analysis, but automation is still limited" [25] (Sec. 5, p. 21); AIOps monitoring can free IT professionals for more innovative tasks (Sec. 4.3.1, p. 15); LLM challenges now center on "the trustworthiness of the results" (Sec. 4.1.4, p. 12)

Authors acknowledge relevant manuscripts may have been missed by the automated process, and gray literature was excluded (Sec. 3.2, p. 9); geographical skew (~51% Europe, none from South America/Africa) plausibly due to query alignment (Sec. 3.3, p. 9); AIOps manuscripts are scarce/underrepresented, so challenges cannot yet be distinguished from MLOps ones — future AIOps literature should enable this; "the recent upsurge in LLMs will spread to MLOps and AIOps, and further analysis on this subject will be necessary" (Sec. 6, p. 22); AIOps use in ML-lifecycle stages such as deployment remains underrepresented (Abstract, p. 1; Sec. 4.4, p. 18)

This SLR provides the methodological and conceptual backdrop for the thesis: it formalizes AIOps as AI aimed at reducing human intervention in IT operations and maps where AIOps already touches incident response (anomaly detection, root cause analysis, log-based remediation, proactive incident triage, ITSM incident prediction/resolution). Its finding that AIOps automation is still limited and detection/RCA-centric substantiates the gap an agentic copilot for MTTD/MTTR reduction would fill. The explicit call to analyze the LLM upsurge in AIOps directly motivates LLM-based agentic copilots as a next step. Its Kitchenham/PRISMA protocol (automated Scopus search, staged screening, quality metrics) is a reusable template for the thesis SLR, though it offers no incident metrics or agent architectures to reuse.
Medium — a foundational AIOps/MLOps survey that frames incident management, observability, and the AIOps-LLM gap, but it measures no MTTD/MTTR and contains no agentic or multi-agent approach.
